questions.q: What is the primary data security dimension used by Payables and Receivables?
options: Balancing segment value
User locale
Business unit
Privilege name
questions.explain: Payables, Receivables, and Procurement primarily scope data security by business unit, since transactions are created and owned within a specific business unit.

questions.q: Which task is used to assign a user access to a specific business unit alongside a job role?
options: Define Chart of Accounts
Manage Data Access for Users
Manage Bank Statements
Create Journal Approval Rules
questions.explain: Manage Data Access for Users, with the security context set to Business Unit, is used to grant a user access to a specific business unit.

questions.q: An AP Specialist at Castellan Robotics has business unit access to US Operations only. What does that access alone grant?
options: Full visibility into every ledger in the company
Automatic access to the General Ledger journal entries those invoices eventually create
Nothing, since business unit access requires a data access set too
The ability to create and manage invoices for the US Operations business unit
questions.explain: Business unit access scopes which business unit's transactions a user can work with in the subledger; it does not automatically grant visibility into General Ledger.

questions.q: Why does a Senior Accountant who already has US Operations business unit access still need a separate grant to review journal entries in General Ledger?
options: General Ledger access is never granted to anyone
Business unit access always includes full ledger access automatically
Business unit access and ledger-level data access sets are separate grants that don't carry over into each other
Journal entries don't require any security at all
questions.explain: Business unit access (subledger-side) and data access sets (ledger-side) are related but distinct grants describing the same transactions from two angles — having one does not imply the other.

questions.q: How is a business unit related to a ledger in Oracle Fusion's enterprise structure?
options: Each business unit is associated with a primary ledger for subledger accounting purposes
They are unrelated and never connected
A ledger can only ever have one business unit, ever
Business units replace the need for a ledger entirely
questions.explain: Each business unit is associated with a primary ledger (and its chart of accounts and calendar), which is how subledger transactions ultimately get accounted for in General Ledger.
